item.title: Supreme Court Blocks Grant Cuts, Air Traffic Stalls: On Air, November 17, 2026
item.description:
The United States Supreme Court on Monday rejected an appeal by the Trump administration seeking to cancel tens of millions of dollars in academic research grants awarded to University of California faculty. The justices issued a brief order without noted dissents, leaving intact a preliminary injunction issued by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. The San Francisco-based appeals court held that federal agencies likely violated the First Amendment by terminating funding based on perceived viewpoints. The grants directly before the Supreme Court were awarded to University of California researchers by the National Science Foundation and the National Endowment for the Humanities.
Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping met Tuesday in Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit to agree on additional tariff cuts and deeper economic ties. China will provide tariff relief on approximately 400 million Canadian dollars, equivalent to 280 million US dollars, in Canadian exports, including frozen pork cuts, fish, and seafood. In exchange, Canada will extend tariff exemptions for specific Chinese steel and aluminum products by two years.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Monday that he is dissolving the NYPD Strategic Response Group, a specialized counterterrorism and protest response unit formed in 2015. Appearing alongside Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, Mamdani stated that the unit will be replaced by a civilian-led Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division within the Mayor Office of Community Safety, alongside a specialized NYPD team named the First Amendment Support Team. The new civilian division possesses no weapons or arrest powers, while the directive bans the use of tear gas, pepper spray, long guns, and kettling during First Amendment activities.
United Airlines resolved a widespread system outage on Monday evening that briefly grounded departing flights across the United States. The technology issue began around 3:30 p.m. and lasted for approximately 90 minutes before systems were restored around 6 p.m. Eastern time. The disruption affected pilot-facing applications, including crew communications and messaging systems, and prevented the airline from providing final aircraft weight information required for preflight calculations. Airborne flights and United Express regional services were unaffected by the outage.
U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz for the Southern District of Texas issued formal warning letters to congressional Democrats, threatening potential legal consequences over upcoming oversight investigations targeting President Donald Trump and his associates. Reitz accused Senator Elizabeth Warren, Senator Richard Blumenthal, Senator Elissa Slotkin, and Representative Robert Garcia of attempting to weaponize congressional oversight and deprive American citizens of constitutional rights. The Campaign for Accountability filed an ethics complaint against Reitz with the State Bar of Texas over the prosecutor's threats.
President Donald Trump landed in the Philippines on Tuesday for a meeting with regional partners and the first gathering of Quad leaders in two years. The visit precedes a trip to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum and a trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. President Trump stated that nuclear disarmament, Ukraine, and Iran would be on the agenda for the discussions in China.

The deployment follows months of stalled diplomatic efforts and a collapsed memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran.

item.title: Brexit Rejected, Drones Strike Crimea, Trade Pacts Strained: On Air, November 16, 2026
item.description:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham prepares to deliver a foreign policy address at the Lord Mayor's Banquet in London, declaring that Brexit has not worked and that the United Kingdom has lost more than it gained since leaving the European Union. Burnham outlines three tests for entering any fresh agreement with the bloc ahead of a summit in Brussels scheduled for November 20. Under these criteria, any agreement must remain within Labour manifesto red lines ruling out membership in the European Union single market, customs union, and freedom of movement.
Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of Crimea, announces the establishment of an emergency headquarters in Kerch, stating vehicular movement would be curtailed until midday following a drone strike. Pro-Ukrainian monitoring group Crimean Wind reports a drone hit one of the bridge arches at 5:38 a.m. local time, while Russian transport authorities note that railway operations resume following brief disruptions that delay four passenger trains between two and four and a half hours. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov describes the damage to the bridge as minor with basic traffic functioning, whereas Russia's Defense Ministry states that air defense units intercept 1,336 Ukrainian drones across Russian regions and occupied territories overnight.
Japan's gross domestic product shrinks at an annualized rate of 0.1 percent in the third quarter of 2026, marking the first economic contraction in four quarters. Real private consumption falls by 0.3 percent quarter-on-quarter, matching the contraction recorded in the prior three months as consumer subsidies on domestic energy expire. Rising energy prices driven by Middle East conflict and a weak yen trading near 160 per US dollar push September core inflation to 2.1 percent, exceeding the central bank target.
The Southern Armed Forces, allied with Yemen's internationally recognized government, complete a withdrawal from positions near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, pulling back toward the interim capital of Aden. Military units vacate Dhubab Airport and coastal sites overlooking the Red Sea transit corridor to reinforce defensive perimeters around Aden and adjacent governorates. Houthi forces move into the evacuated territory, extending control over the waterway and reaching positions within 60 kilometers of Aden.
José Maria Neves wins re-election in Cape Verde with approximately 63.8 percent of the provisional vote, surpassing the 50 percent threshold needed to prevent a runoff. Main challenger Joana Rosa, the country's first female presidential candidate, places second with roughly 31.6 percent of the vote and concedes defeat. Voter turnout is recorded at approximately 32 percent across more than 419,000 registered voters.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney states that Canada could partner with Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with United States President Donald Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry. Carney makes the statements in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, ahead of a scheduled meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen. Canada previously reached an agreement in January permitting tens of thousands of Chinese electric vehicles to enter the country at reduced tariff rates.
Estonian authorities announce that all border crossings with Russia will close on December 1 following a thwarted arson attack at Threod Systems, a defense company and drone manufacturer located north of Tallinn in Viimsi. Intruders smash windows and attempt to pour flammable liquids into the premises shortly after 3 a.m. on Saturday.
